candidates.decision_relevance: Several reviews explicitly cannot determine whether breadth, ETH/BTC, price, liquidity, and flow deterioration preceded drawdowns or appeared afterward. A synchronized historical sequence would make freeze-time and lead-lag analyses possible without relying on completed-week endpoints.
candidates.evidence_reference: Weekly reviews W37–W43 note missing common-timeline observations and freeze-time sequences; daily outputs report 168 hourly ETH/BTC closes but repeatedly lack comparable historical sequences across other measures.
candidates.metric_name: Timestamp-aligned price, ETH/BTC, and available breadth/flow observations
candidates.missing_history_problem: The supplied analyses mostly provide endpoint summaries, overlapping windows, or snapshots with different capture times and universes. Prior hourly records on a consistent timeline are absent, so sequence, persistence, and decision-time availability cannot be reconstructed.

candidates.decision_relevance: Breadth is repeatedly cited as potentially important to distinguishing broad participation from narrow leadership, but point-in-time proxy captures have changing memberships and often lack a path. A historical constituent-level record would permit consistent-universe and cross-sectional participation checks.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily outputs repeatedly flag differing membership hashes and missing canonical breadth history; W37 reviews specifically lack the construction, universe, and timestamp of breadth observations.
candidates.metric_name: Constituent-level breadth observations with timestamp and universe membership
candidates.missing_history_problem: Available breadth values are isolated proxy snapshots, often incomparable across captures. Without prior membership-aware observations, persistence and breadth changes cannot be separated from universe turnover or endpoint selection.

candidates.decision_relevance: Analyses repeatedly describe ETF evidence as a single settled session, divergent across BTC and ETH, or missing a within-week sequence. Historical daily settled rows would allow flow persistence and sequencing relative to price and participation to be examined.
candidates.evidence_reference: W39–W43 reviews and daily outputs state that settled ETF sequences are unavailable or limited to one reported session; W37 review notes positive ETH flows but lacks aligned timing.
candidates.metric_name: Daily settled BTC and ETH ETF flow observations
candidates.missing_history_problem: Sparse settled rows do not establish whether flows persisted, changed before or after market weakness, or were isolated sessions. Missing sessions are explicitly not imputed in the supplied analyses.

candidates.decision_relevance: Reviews identify the absence of prospective warning timestamps and linked matured paths as preventing assessment of premature versus late recognition. Timestamped freeze observations linked to subsequent price paths would support historical path and horizon analysis without treating overlapping freezes as independent events.
candidates.evidence_reference: W39–W43 reviews report zero eligible prospective typed warning rows or missing warning-linked outcomes, and repeatedly caution that overlapping freezes and completed-week paths cannot establish warning timing.
candidates.metric_name: Point-in-time warning-observation snapshots linked to subsequent asset price paths
candidates.missing_history_problem: The supplied protection summaries are descriptive aggregates, often have no eligible typed warning series, and do not preserve the information available at each freeze alongside its later path. This prevents direct timing and opportunity-cost evaluation.
